## Summary

During the civil war between the MPLA government and UNITA, and with an economy living on oil, the state paid for the war with the central bank. The kwanza was reformed three times in a decade. Hyperinflation in the strict sense ran from **December 1994 to January 1997**. It peaked at **84.1 % in May 1996, doubling every 34.5 days** (H&K).

## Causes

- **War.** The civil war (1975–2002) resumed after the 1992 election.

## Timeline

- **25 Sep 1990** — the novo kwanza; people may exchange only 5 % of their old notes, so most
  savings are wiped out at a stroke.
- **1991** — a 500,000-kwanza note.
- **Dec 1994** — monthly inflation passes 50 % (H&K start).
- **1 Jul 1995** — the kwanza reajustado (1,000 : 1).
- **May 1996** — the peak, 84.1 % (H&K).
- **Jan 1997** — the H&K episode ends.
- **1 Dec 1999** — the kwanza (1,000,000 : 1).
- **2002** — the war ends.

## Lessons

- A currency reform that confiscates (only 5 % exchangeable) destroys trust in the next one.
